I have farmed this land in Quzhou for 45 years. I know every mu of it. At 63, with just my wife and me in the household, I must be honest about what two old bodies can manage. Cotton pays well when the price is right, but picking it by hand is backbreaking work that takes us into the cold of autumn. I cannot handle more than a small plot of it anymore. Most of my ground—30 mu—will stay in the wheat-maize rotation I have done for decades. The wheat is already in the field from last October; it needs a good top-dressing of nitrogen at green-up, two or three irrigations from our well, and a spray or two for weeds and bugs. When we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste. We will burn the stubble or chop it, and plant the summer maize right away with a no-tillage seeder. The maize will get its base fertilizer at sowing, a sidedress of urea when it is knee-high, and two irrigations if the summer rains are stingy. For the 4.5 mu of cotton, we will rotary-till in April, lay down the plastic mulch like we always do, and plant hybrid Bt cotton to save on some spraying. It will need more potash than the grain crops to keep the bolls strong, and three good irrigations—at planting, flowering, and boll-opening. I expect the wheat to give me about 460 jin per mu, the maize about 580 jin per mu, and the cotton about 270 jin of seed cotton per mu if the weather treats us fairly.
